external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: Developers who push branches to the self-hosted git server and can log in to the build runner to initiate a rebuild.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: Public package registry on the internet reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the image registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be used to initiate a manual rebuild.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The runner uses a shared build token to call the deploy controller. It does not verify signatures on downloads from the public package registry.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Controller on the corporate network that receives release requests and answers store servers' current-release queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network
processes.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office running the till software as a container. It polls the deploy controller, pulls a changed image, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: The description covers about 1,200 store servers.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: Git server on the corporate network holding developer branches and source used by builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: Registry in the build environment holding finished container images tagged with commit SHA values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows store-server pulls, but what a store server presents to it has not been documented.

data_stores.name: current release record
data_stores.description: The record held by the deploy controller identifying which image SHA the estate should be on.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developer pushes a branch to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: Build runner fetches source after a merge starts a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: Build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit SHA.
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with commit SHA

data_flows.name: make current release
data_flows.description: Build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: image SHA to set as current release

data_flows.name: ask current release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller what the current release is once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull, but nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: Build runner reaches out to the public package registry during dependency resolution.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: dependencies downloaded according to the lockfile

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually initiates a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Corporate network containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: Separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: In-store estate containing the store servers running the till software.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: Public internet zone containing the public package registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The build runner contains or handles credentials and secrets because it uses the shared build token to call the deploy controller.
assumptions.basis: The description states that the runner uses a shared build token to call the deploy controller.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller handles business-critical data because it controls the image release for the estate.
assumptions.basis: The controller holds the release record that determines which image the estate should run.

assumptions.assumption: The store server and till software are availability-critical because they run the till software in each store.
assumptions.basis: Each store server runs the till software, and the software is part of the in-store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The till software is availability-critical because it is the software running the store tills.
assumptions.basis: The text identifies it as the till software running in each store.

assumptions.assumption: The self-hosted git server holds business-critical data because it stores developer branches and source used to build the estate software.
assumptions.basis: Developers push branches to it and the build runner fetches source from it.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry holds business-critical data because it stores the container image deployed across the store estate.
assumptions.basis: The finished image is pushed to the registry and pulled by store servers for deployment.

assumptions.assumption: The current release record is business-critical data because it determines which image the estate should run.
assumptions.basis: The record states which image SHA the estate should be on.

assumptions.assumption: The dependency-resolution flow carries business-critical data because it concerns dependencies used to produce the deployed container image.
assumptions.basis: The flow downloads dependencies used by the build runner to produce a container image.

assumptions.assumption: The manual rebuild flow concerns business-critical data because it initiates a rebuild of main.
assumptions.basis: The text states that a developer can kick off a rebuild of main.
